final_assessment: Consume-mode propose from an exploration with eight decisions and zero open questions, so no prompts fired. The change is a SUBTRACTION: clause (c) retired from the convergence criterion, and the budget signal demoted to a recorded figure per Q-crc-19. Two decisions were taken AT PROPOSE and recorded in design.md rather than smuggled in: D2, that the readiness obligation replacing clause (c) is NOT shipped here because a requirement demanding a record no command yet writes would fail every gate — which is the very defect being removed, so rc02c subtracts and rc04 adds; and D4, that `stands` is not shipped, because it would give a recorded fact a writer before it has a reader, the write-only pattern this repo has now logged three times. A third, D4b, came from an error caught in flight: renaming the budget requirement's header broke the MODIFIED match, and `orbit fingerprint` reported 'requirement not found in live baseline' while `orbit validate --strict` passed. The title was reverted; a rename would be a RENAMED operation no archived change here has exercised, and a mismatched MODIFIED header ADDS a second requirement beside the original rather than replacing it. Scenario accounting is deliberate and auditable rather than silent: 25 to 22 on the convergence requirement (three removed asserting the retired selection rule and predicate, one rewritten as a clause-(b) fact) and 14 to 12 on the budget requirement (two removed asserting exhaustion precedence, two rewritten), with the removals named inside each delta. Six base fingerprints stamped. SIZE: 2 capabilities, 7 requirements, 15 tasks — all inside R-crc-1 — and 56.1 KB of delta, over the ~40 KB byte line. That overage was measured, examined, and accepted rather than ignored: the ceiling's byte figure was calibrated on c2, an ADDED-heavy change where bytes meant new design surface, whereas this change is MODIFIED-heavy and its bytes are dominated by verbatim scenario preservation that C2's discipline requires. New-or-changed prose is roughly 10 KB. R-crc-1 itself states that capabilities predict cost better than bytes, and on that axis this sits at 2 of 3. Recorded for rc09-propose-hygiene, which owns automating this check: the byte dimension needs to be MODIFIED-aware or it will keep flagging subtractive changes as oversized.
